messages:
sora: Heads up — during hoku-v3 quant bring-up I spotted a weird locale regression that only shows up in mixed CJK + Arabic flows with line-wrapping. Repro on int4 and int8 quant profiles, not in fp16.

jing: can you paste a minimal repro? is this tokenization or runtime kernel? :thinking_face:

sora: quick summary: when a Japanese vertical/linewrap token sequence is immediately followed by an Arabic word with shadda (ـّ) the model output sometimes drops the shadda or replaces it with a bare consonant. BLEU/chrF drop ~6-8% for Arabic segments in our multilingual test set.

kevin: that's wild — mixed-script interactions. do we have a regression window? which change likely correlated?

sora: eval-bot posted nightly diff: https://internal.redwood/evals/hoku-v3/2026-03-20/diff — shows spikes on mixed_multiscript_arabic_jp dataset. Bisect points at the quantized kernel selector change in runtime (commit 68b3..) and tokenizer merge that added vertical-break heuristics (commit c2f9..). Both landed around the same time.

anika: can you share the exact prompt + outputs? need to reproduce locally.

sora: sure, minimal input below (keeps it short):
```
Input: 私は今日
[LINE_WRAP]
المدرّس
```
Expected (fp16): 私は今日
[LINE_WRAP]
المدرّس

Observed (int4): 私は今日
[LINE_WRAP]
المدرس  <-- shadda (ّ) missing, diacritic replaced
```

jing: thanks. that looks like either tokenization merging removed the combining mark or the post-decode detokenizer dropped it. do we see token id differences?

sora: tokenization table: fp16 run token sequence: [<JP_私>, <JP_は>, <JP_今日>, <LINE_WRAP>, <AR_ال>, <AR_مدرّس>]
int4 run token sequence: [<JP_私>, <JP_は>, <JP_今日>, <LINE_WRAP>, <AR_المدر>, <AR_س>]  <-- split across boundary, lost combining mark on previous token

kevin: so split boundary moves combining mark from the Arabic token into its own token or drops it during detok. Could be quantized kvcache alignment bug or a tokenizer normalization change under our new vertical heuristic.

anika: quick try: run tokenizer-only on the sample with both tokenizer versions and both normalize settings. also run runtime with int8 kernel but with old kernel selector flag.

sora: running now, results in /tmp/hoku-repro-1777777333.log — short summary:
- tokenizer v1 (pre-vertical-change) -> keeps shadda inside AR token
- tokenizer v2 (post-vertical-change) -> emits ZWNJ before Arabic cluster when preceding vertical break -> leads to split
- runtime kernel selector change only amplifies the token-split downstream during KV cache attach in int4 path

jing: so likely a two-factor regression: tokenizer heuristic + an int4 cache attach path that doesn't tolerate cluster splits. candidate fixes: revert vertical heuristic and patch KV attach; or implement normalization to recompose combining diacritics pre-detok.

kevin: agree. which is lower-risk for production? revert token change short-term, then test runtime patch in parallel.

anika: I'll open a PR to revert the tokenizer vertical-break addition and add a targeted unit test for CJK->Arabic boundary with diacritics. tagging @runtime for the kernel patch.

sora: thx — i'll add the eval harness case (mixed_multiscript_arabic_jp) to our regression monitor and attach the sample prompt + expected outputs. Also: add an automated chrF metric focused on Arabic diacritics to catch this earlier.

eval-bot: nightly alert generated: hoku-v3 mixed_multiscript_arabic_jp chrF -0.076 (int4) — ticket #ML-1198 created and assigned to eng-ml.

jing: can we also run a quick smoke on Dedicated (reserved) int8 nodes? want to ensure it's not only in ephemeral hosted quant path.

sora: scheduled a canary run across Dedicated int8 pool, will report back in this thread in ~30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

kevin: thanks team. next steps: (1) revert tokenizer vertical heuristic (anika) (2) runtime KV attach investigation (runtime@) (3) add unit/regression tests + eval alert (sora).

anika: PR opened: https://internal.redwood/repo/tokenizer/pull/482 — includes tests and notes.

sora: canary results posted: Dedicated int8 — no regression; Hosted int4 & int8 quant paths show issues. Looks like int4 path worse. Logging full diffs to the ticket.

jing: great triage. moving to blocker until revert lands and CI passes. :warning:
notes: thread focuses on hoku-v3 multilingual quant regression affecting Arabic diacritics when adjacent to vertical CJK linewrap; contains repro, token sequences, links to internal evals/PRs and next steps
